subject: history_social
passage: Around 1200 BCE, many of the powerful kingdoms of the eastern Mediterranean, including the Hittite Empire and the Mycenaean palace states of Greece, collapsed within a few decades. Egyptian inscriptions from the period describe attacks by seaborne raiders, whom modern scholars call the Sea Peoples, and for much of the twentieth century historians treated these invaders as the main cause of the catastrophe.
passage_b: Archaeologist Nadia Haddad doubts that any single cause can account for so widespread a collapse. Evidence from lake sediments and ancient pollen points to a prolonged drought in the region at about this time, and several cities show signs of earthquake damage. Because the kingdoms depended on one another for grain, tin, and copper, she argues, troubles in one place spread to others, and the raids of the Sea Peoples may have been as much a symptom of the crisis as its cause.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view held by historians in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that drought, rather than any invasion, was the sole cause of the kingdoms' collapse
choices.B: By dismissing the Egyptian inscriptions as unreliable evidence that raids occurred
choices.C: By suggesting that the raids were part of a broader crisis with several causes
choices.D: By agreeing that the Sea Peoples were the primary cause of the kingdoms' decline

explanation.why: Twentieth-century historians in Text 1 treated the Sea Peoples as "the main cause." Haddad doubts "that any single cause can account for" the collapse, citing drought, earthquakes, and trade connections, and says the raids "may have been as much a symptom of the crisis as its cause." So she would place the raids within a wider, many-sided crisis.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Haddad rejects any single cause, so she would not name drought as the sole cause.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 does not question whether the raids happened; it questions how much they explain.
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 presents drought, earthquakes, and linked economies as causes and treats the raids as possibly a symptom of the larger crisis.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the view Text 2 challenges.
